01Best System Design Resources

Repo kya hai — shuruaat yahan se

Ye repo 100+ best System Design resources ka ek hi jagah par jama kiya hua collection hai — online courses, books, websites, cheat sheets, interview questions, practice problems, case studies, tutorials, papers aur engineering blogs. Senior Engineer, Lead ya Architect role ke liye prepare kar rahe ho to System Design round sabse important hota hai — aur ye repo usi ki taiyaari ka poora map hai.

System Design interview itna mushkil kyun hai

System Design interview open-ended hota hai — iska koi ek sahi jawab nahi hota. Sawal bada hota hai ("YouTube design karo"), aur tumhe requirements samajhni hain, scale ka andaza lagana hai, components chunne hain, trade-offs batane hain aur bottlenecks pehchanne hain. Isi vastness ki wajah se taiyaari mushkil lagti hai, lekin is round ko ignore bhi nahi kar sakte — senior roles me ye decide karta hai ki offer milega ya nahi.

Is repo ka tareeka — checklist

Repo ke author ne apni khud ki taiyaari ke dauraan ek checklist banayi thi, jo unke interviews me kaam aayi. Usi soch par ye repo bana hai: pehle structured courses se seekho, phir books se gehrai me jao, phir basics aur questions par haath saaf karo, phir problems practice karo, aur aakhir me cheat sheets se revise karo. Is SPA me har section ke saath Hinglish explanation hai, aur har resource ka original link bhi hai — link par click karte hi original source khul jayega.

Is SPA me kya-kya hai

  • Courses (14) — structured tareeke se seekhne ke liye sabse achhe online courses
  • Books (11) — gehrai wala knowledge, interview crack karne ke liye
  • Seekhne ki jagah (17) — platforms aur websites jahan seekh bhi sakte ho aur practice bhi
  • Basics (34 concepts) — har concept ki Hinglish samajh
  • Interview questions (10 + 7) — aksar puche jaane wale concept questions
  • Practice problems (14) — YouTube, WhatsApp, Instagram jaise mashhoor problems
  • Case studies, tutorials, fundamentals, papers, patterns — gehrai ke liye
  • Cheat sheets (5) — aakhri waqt ki revision ke liye, images ke saath
  • Engineering blogs (35) — company blogs jahan real architecture padhne ko milta hai
  • Aur resources (26 links) — extra articles aur guides
Ek zaroori baat: is repo ke saare links bahari websites, courses aur books ki taraf jaate hain. Ye SPA har concept ko Hinglish me samjhata hai aur har link ko bachakar rakhta hai — lekin poori paid courses ya poori kitabein is SPA ke andar nahi hain, wo unke original sources par hain. Ye baat Trust Check ke out-of-scope list me saaf likhi hai.

02Best System Design Resources

Taiyaari ka plan — kis stage par kya karo

Repo khud koi fixed timetable nahi deta — lekin uski structure se ek saaf kram nikalta hai. Neeche wala plan is SPA ka suggested kram hai, jo repo ke sections ki tartib par based hai. Apne paas kitna time hai, us hisaab se stage chuno.

Stage 1 — Shuruaat (pehle 1-2 hafte)

Bilkul zero se shuru kar rahe ho to pehle ek structured course lo — Section 03 se ByteByteGo, Codemia ya Exponent me se koi ek chuno. Saath-saath Section 06 ke System Design Basics ke pehle 10 concepts padho (API Gateway, Load Balancer, scaling, caching, rate limiter). Roz ek concept, uski Hinglish samajh aur uska linked article.

Stage 2 — Gehrai (agle 2-4 hafte)

Ab books uthao — Section 04 se pehle System Design Interview wali kitab, phir Designing Data-Intensive Applications. Saath me Section 07 ke 10 interview questions aur Section 08 ke theory questions ke jawab khud se bol-bol kar practice karo. Har jawab me framework yaad rakho: requirements → scale ka andaza → API → high-level design → deep-dive → bottlenecks → trade-offs.

Stage 3 — Practice (agle 2-3 hafte)

Section 09 ke 14 problems par haath aazmao — URL Shortener, WhatsApp, Instagram, YouTube se shuru karo. Har problem par 45 minute ka timer lagao, khud se design banao, phir linked solution se compare karo. Section 10-12 ke case studies aur tutorials se real systems kaise scale hue, wo samjho.

Stage 4 — Aakhri hafta (revision)

Section 16 ki cheat sheets print karke revise karo. Section 14 ke Dynamo paper ke core ideas aur Section 13 ke data structures (Bloom Filter, Gossip) ek baar phir dekh lo. Mock interviews do — Exponent ya Bugfree.ai par. Aur jis company me interview hai, uske engineering blog (Section 17) se uski architecture padh lo — interview me bahut kaam aata hai.

Honest note: upar wala plan repo me aise likha hua nahi hai — ye is SPA ne repo ke sections ki tartib aur uske "starting from scratch vs a week out" wale idea se banaya hai. Repo ka asal content courses, books aur links hain; plan unhe use karne ka tareeka hai.

Best System Design Courses (14)

Online courses taiyaari ka sabse structured tareeka hain. Neeche repo ke saare 14 courses hain — har ek ke saath Hinglish me bataya hai ki wo kis cheez ke liye best hai. Link par click karte hi course khul jayega.

  1. ByteByteGo — Visual guides aur gehri explanation. Diagrams se concepts samajhne ke liye sabse achha. Newsletter aur courses dono hain.
  2. Codemia.io — LeetCode-style System Design prep. Questions solve karke seekhne walo ke liye.
  3. Exponent — Peers ke saath free System Design mock interviews. Asli interview jaisi practice ke liye.
  4. Grokking the System Design Interview (DesignGuru) — Classic course, interview problems ke step-by-step solutions ke liye mashhoor.
  5. Bugfree.ai — System Design practice questions aur AI-based mock interviews.
  6. System Design School — Interactive System Design prep.
  7. System Design Masterclass (Udemy) — Video course, poora masterclass format.
  8. Grokking Modern System Design (Educative) — Interactive, text-based course + AI mock interviews.
  9. Modern System Design Course (Udemy) — Udemy par modern System Design prep.
  10. Advanced System Design Course (DesignGuru) — Grokking ke aage, advanced level ke liye.
  11. Zero to Mastery Academy — Bootcamp-style learning.
  12. Meetapro — Mentorship aur interview prep platform.
  13. Software Design Specialization (Coursera) — University of Alberta ka specialization, software architecture par.
  14. Software Architecture 101 — Architecture ke fundamentals par course.
Kaise chuno: pehli baar prepare kar rahe ho to ek visual course (ByteByteGo) + ek practice platform (Codemia ya Exponent) ka combo best hai. Sirf videos dekhna kaafi nahi — har course ke saath khud problems solve karo.

04Best System Design Resources

Best System Design Books (11)

Courses se shuruaat achhi hoti hai, lekin interview crack karne wali gehrai kitabo se aati hai. Neeche repo ki saari 11 kitabein hain — har ek ke saath bataya hai ki wo kya cover karti hai aur kis ke liye hai.

  1. Designing Data-Intensive Applications — Data systems ki bible. Storage, replication, partitioning, transactions, stream processing — jo bhi data se juda hai, isme gehrai se hai. Senior interviews ke liye must-read. Note: README me iska naam galti se "Data-Insensitive" likha hai — sahi naam "Data-Intensive" hai.
  2. System Design Interview — Sabse pehle padhne wali kitab. Interview framework aur classic problems (TinyURL, chat, newsfeed) ke step-by-step solutions.
  3. The System Design Interview, 2nd Edition — Interview framework aur problems ka doosra edition, updated content ke saath.
  4. System Design Interview — An Insider's Guide: Volume 2 — Volume 1 ke aage — aur problems, aur gehrai, real interview jaisi depth.
  5. Machine Learning System Design Interview — ML system design interviews ke liye — ML models ko production system me kaise design karte hain.
  6. Hacking the System Design Interview — Real big-tech interview questions aur unke in-depth solutions.
  7. Acing the System Design Interview — Interview me top karne ke liye practical approach aur techniques.
  8. The System Design Interview, 2nd Edition — Upar wali #3 se alag kitab hai, isi naam se — isme bhi framework aur problems hain, alag approach ke saath.
  9. System Design at Google: Engineering Peak for Interviews — Google-style interviews par focused.
  10. Mastering the System Design Interview — Ek former hiring manager ke insider tips — interviewer kya dekhta hai, ye samajhne ke liye.
Honest note: README me 11 kitabein list hain, lekin "Machine Learning System Design Interview" do baar aayi hai (item 5 aur item 9, ek hi link) — isliye upar 10 unique kitabein dikhayi gayi hain. Aur kitabo ke lekhako ke naam is SPA me nahi likhe gaye hain — sirf kitab ke naam aur links hain.

Kis order me padho: pehle #2 (System Design Interview), phir #1 (Designing Data-Intensive Applications) — ye do kitabein milkar 80% taiyaari kar deti hain. ML roles ke liye #5 add karo.

Pichhla04 Best System Design Books (11)Agla06 System Design Basics — 34 zaroori concepts
06Best System Design Resources

System Design Basics — 34 zaroori concepts

Ye woh essential concepts hain jo har programmer ko aane chahiye. Har concept ke saath Hinglish samajh hai — kaise kaam karta hai, kab use karte hain, aur kya trade-offs hain. Jahan README ne link diya hai, wo bhi saath me hai.

01 — API Gateway vs Load Balancer

API Gateway ek single entry point hai — saare client requests pehle is par aate hain. Ye authentication, rate limiting, request routing aur response transformation karta hai. Load Balancer traffic ko multiple servers me baant-ta hai taaki koi ek server overload na ho. Dono saath me kaam karte hain: Gateway pehle, phir Load Balancer. Detail me padho

02 — Reverse Proxy vs Forward Proxy

Forward Proxy client ki taraf hota hai — client ki identity chhupata hai, content filter karta hai. Reverse Proxy server ki taraf hota hai — server ki identity chhupata hai, load balancing aur caching karta hai. Interview me dono ka difference aur use-case poochte hain. Detail me padho

03 — Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling

Vertical scaling matlab ek hi machine ko powerful banao (zyada RAM/CPU) — aasan hai lekin ek limit ke baad mehenga aur risky (single point of failure). Horizontal scaling matlab aur machines jodo — mushkil hai (data sync, load balancing chahiye) lekin practically unlimited aur fault-tolerant. Aaj ke systems horizontal scaling par chalte hain. Detail me padho

04 — Microservices vs Monolithic Architecture

Monolith me poora app ek hi codebase aur ek hi deploy unit me hota hai — shuruaat me tez aur simple. Microservices me app chhote-chhote independent services me tootta hai — har service alag deploy, alag scale hoti hai. Trade-off: microservices me flexibility milti hai, lekin complexity (network calls, distributed transactions, monitoring) badh jaati hai. Chhote app ke liye monolith, bade aur fast-changing system ke liye microservices. Detail me padho

05 — Caching Strategies

Cache matlab frequently use hone wala data fast memory (RAM) me rakhna taaki database ko baar-baar na poochna pade. Strategies: Cache-Aside (app pehle cache dekhti hai, miss hone par DB se laati hai), Write-Through (likhte hi cache aur DB dono update), Write-Behind (pehle cache, baad me DB — tez lekin risk), Read-Through. Cache invalidation (purana data kab hatayein) sabse mushkil hissa hai. Detail me padho

06 — Rate Limiter: kya hai, kaise kaam karta hai

Rate Limiter ek user/IP ko ek time me kitne requests karne deta hai, use control karta hai — taaki ek user poora system down na kar de aur abuse ruke. Algorithms: Token Bucket (bucket me token bharte rehte hain, har request ek token kharch karti hai), Leaky Bucket (fixed rate se requests process), Fixed Window Counter, Sliding Window. Interview me aksar "Rate Limiter design karo" poochte hain. Detail me padho

07 — Single Sign-On (SSO) kaise kaam karta hai

SSO matlab ek baar login karo, saari connected apps me access mil jaye (jaise ek Google login se Gmail, YouTube, Drive). Kaam aise karta hai: tum Identity Provider par login karte ho, wo ek token deta hai, aur har app us token ko verify karke tumhe andar jaane deti hai. Protocols: SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect. Detail me padho

08 — Apache Kafka kaise kaam karta hai, aur itna fast kyun hai

Kafka ek distributed event streaming platform hai — producers messages bhejte hain, topics me store hote hain, consumers padhte hain. Fast kyun hai: sequential disk writes (random writes se 100x tez), zero-copy (data bina copy kiye network par bhejna), batching aur partitioning (parallel processing). Detail me padho

09 — Kafka vs ActiveMQ vs RabbitMQ

Teeno message brokers hain, kaam alag hai: Kafka high-throughput event streaming ke liye (logs, real-time data pipelines). RabbitMQ traditional message queue — routing, acknowledgements aur complex workflows ke liye best. ActiveMQ purana, Java/JMS ecosystem ke liye. Interview me "kab kaunsa" poochte hain — jawab throughput aur use-case par based hota hai. Detail me padho

10 — JWT, OAuth aur SAML

JWT ek token format hai — user ki info signed JSON me hoti hai, server bina DB pooche verify kar sakta hai. OAuth 2.0 ek authorization framework hai — "is app ko mere Google data ki permission do" wala flow. SAML enterprise SSO ka purana standard hai (XML-based). Teeno alag cheezein hain: JWT = token, OAuth = permission dene ka tareeka, SAML = enterprise login protocol. Detail me padho

11 — Database Scaling

Database badi hone par kya karte hain: pehle vertical scaling (bada server), phir read replicas (reads alag servers par), phir sharding (data ko tukdo me baant kar alag servers par), aur caching (database tak requests hi kam pahunchein). Har step ke trade-offs hain — sharding se joins mushkil ho jaate hain, replicas se data thoda purana dikh sakta hai. Detail me padho

12 — Database Replication vs Sharding

Replication matlab data ki copy multiple servers par — reads tez hote hain, aur ek server down ho to dusra kaam aata hai. Sharding matlab data ko tukdo (shards) me baantna — har shard par data ka ek hissa hota hai, total capacity badhti hai. Dono ek saath bhi use hote hain: har shard ke apne replicas. Detail me padho

13 — JWT vs Session-based Authentication

Session me server user ki login state apne paas rakhta hai (memory ya DB me) aur client ko sirf ek session ID deta hai. JWT me state client ke paas hoti hai — token me hi saari info hoti hai, server stateless rehta hai. Session secure aur revoke karna aasan hai; JWT scale karna aasan hai (koi server-side state nahi). Detail me padho

14 — Consistent Hashing

Normal hashing me server add/remove karne par lagbhag saara data dobara map karna padta hai. Consistent Hashing me servers aur keys ko ek circle (hash ring) par rakha jaata hai — server add/remove karne par sirf uske aas-paas ki keys move hoti hain. Caching systems (Memcached, Dynamo) isi par chalte hain. Virtual nodes se load evenly baant-te hain.

15 — Message Queues

Message Queue do services ke beech ka buffer hai — ek service message daalti hai, dusri apne time par nikaal kar process karti hai. Fayda: services loosely coupled rehti hain, traffic spikes absorb ho jaate hain, aur ek service down ho to messages kho nahi jaate. Examples: RabbitMQ, SQS, Kafka. Detail me padho

16 — REST vs gRPC

REST HTTP + JSON par chalta hai — simple, har jagah supported, browser-friendly. gRPC HTTP/2 + Protocol Buffers par chalta hai — binary format, tez, aur streaming support karta hai, lekin browser me seedha use nahi hota. Internal service-to-service communication ke liye gRPC, public APIs ke liye REST zyada common hai. Detail me padho

17 — Leader Election (Raft, Paxos)

Distributed system me kaun leader hai (kaun likhega, kaun decide karega), ye decide karne ke liye election hoti hai. Raft simple aur samajhne me aasan consensus algorithm hai — leader, follower aur candidate roles hote hain. Paxos purana aur mushkil, lekin theoretically strong. Etcd, Consul jaise systems Raft use karte hain.

18 — Circuit Breakers

Agar ek service baar-baar fail ho rahi hai, to har baar use call karke time waste karne se behtar hai ki circuit "khol" do — matlab us service ko call karna hi band kar do, aur turant fallback/error do. Kuch time baad circuit "half-open" hota hai — ek try karke dekhta hai ki service wapas aayi ya nahi. Ye pattern cascading failures rokta hai. Detail me padho

19 — Failover aur Disaster Recovery

Failover matlab primary system down hote hi backup system apne aap kaam sambhal le. Disaster Recovery usse bada plan hai — poora data center down ho jaye to bhi system dusri region se chal pade. Iske liye chahiye: data replication across regions, regular backups, aur failover ka rehearsal. RTO (kitni der me wapas) aur RPO (kitna data kho sakta hai) — ye do numbers har DR plan me hote hain.

20 — Heartbeats aur Health Checks

Services ek dusre ko regular "heartbeat" signals bhejti hain — "main zinda hoon". Agar heartbeat aana band ho jaye to system samajh jaata hai ki wo service down hai, aur traffic us taraf bhejna band kar deta hai. Health checks load balancer karta hai — unhealthy server ko rotation se nikaal deta hai.

21 — CQRS

CQRS matlab reads aur writes ke liye alag models. Writes ek model me jaate hain (jo data ko sahi rakhta hai), reads dusre model se hote hain (jo fast queries ke liye optimized hai). Read-heavy systems me bahut fayda deta hai, lekin complexity badhta hai — dono models ko sync rakhna padta hai. Detail me padho

22 — Event-Driven Design

Event-driven design me services seedha ek dusre ko call nahi karti — balki events publish karti hain ("order placed"), aur jo service interested hai wo sun kar apna kaam karti hai. Fayda: loose coupling, aasani se nayi service jod sakte ho. Nuksan: debugging mushkil, aur event order ka dhyaan rakhna padta hai. Detail me padho

23 — Saga Pattern

Microservices me ek kaam multiple services me hota hai — agar beech me ek step fail ho jaye to poora transaction wapas kaise lein? Saga me har step ke saath ek "compensating action" hoti hai (jaise payment fail ho to refund kar do). Do tareeke: choreography (har service event se next ko trigger karti hai) aur orchestration (ek central coordinator sab sambhalta hai). Detail me padho

24 — Idempotency

Idempotent operation matlab use ek baar karo ya 10 baar, result ek hi hota hai. Example: payment ka "pay" button do baar dabne par paise ek hi baar katne chahiye. Iske liye har request ko ek unique idempotency key di jaati hai — dobara wahi key aaye to server pehla result wapas de deta hai, kaam dobara nahi karta. Detail me padho

25 — Cache Invalidation Strategies

Cache ka sabse mushkil sawal: purana data kab hatayein? Tareeke: TTL (time ke baad auto-expire), write-through (likhte hi cache update), event-based (data badalte hi cache clear karo). Galat invalidation se user ko purana data dikhta hai — isliye kehte hain cache invalidation computer science ki sabse mushkil problems me se ek hai. Detail me padho

26 — TCP vs UDP

TCP reliable hai — data order me aur bina khoye pahunchta hai, lekin slow (handshake + acknowledgement). UDP fast hai lekin unreliable — packets kho bhi sakte hain, order bhi bigad sakta hai. Web, email, file transfer = TCP. Video streaming, gaming, DNS = UDP. Detail me padho

27 — APIs, Database aur CDN

Teeno milkar ek web system banta hai: API woh darwaza hai jahan se client system se baat karta hai, Database me data rehta hai, aur CDN static content (images, videos, CSS) ko user ke sabse kareeb wale server se deta hai taaki page tez khule. Interview me aksar poochte hain: "browser me URL type karne par kya hota hai" — jawab in teeno se shuru hota hai. Detail me padho

28 — API Security: 7 zaroori baatein

API secure karne ke liye: authentication (kaun hai), authorization (kya kar sakta hai), rate limiting (kitna kar sakta hai), input validation (galat data na aaye), HTTPS (data encrypt rahe), secrets ko code me hardcode na karo, aur logging/monitoring (kuch galat ho to pata chale). Detail me padho

29 — Microservices Best Practices

Microservices tabhi fayda dete hain jab sahi tareeke se banayein: har service ka ek clear kaam ho, services ke beech API contract fixed ho, har service ka apna database ho, centralized logging aur monitoring ho, aur har service independently deploy ho sake. Bina inke microservices "distributed monolith" ban jaate hain — dono ke nuksan, kisi ka fayda nahi. Detail me padho

30 — OAuth 2.0

OAuth 2.0 se user apna password diye bina kisi app ko apne data ki limited permission de sakta hai — jaise "is app ko meri Google photos dekhne do". Flow: app permission maangti hai → user authorize karta hai → app ko access token milta hai → token se limited kaam hota hai. Detail me padho

31 — Proxies

Proxy beech me baitha server hai jo requests ko forward karta hai. Forward proxy client ki taraf, reverse proxy server ki taraf. Proxies caching, security, load balancing aur anonymity — chaaro kaam aate hain. Detail me padho

32 — Authentication

Authentication matlab "tum kaun ho" verify karna — password, OTP, biometrics, ya SSO se. Authorization uske baad aata hai — "tum kya-kya kar sakte ho". Dono alag hain, aur interview me aksar inka difference poochte hain. Detail me padho

33 — Single Point of Failure (SPOF)

SPOF woh ek component hai jiske down hote hi poora system ruk jaye. System design me pehla kaam hi ye hota hai: SPOF dhoondho aur hatao — redundancy se (backup servers), replication se (data ki copies), aur failover se. Detail me padho

34 — Distributed Caching

Ek machine ka cache chhota padta hai to cache ko bhi distribute karte hain — multiple cache servers, consistent hashing se keys baant-te hain. Redis Cluster aur Memcached isi tareeke se kaam karte hain. Dhyaan rakhne wali baat: cache node down ho to uski keys dobara database se laani padti hain (cache stampede se bachne ke liye warming ya locking use karte hain). Detail me padho

README ki numbering par note: README ki list me numbering 10 ke baad seedha 15 se shuru hoti hai (11-14 missing hain) aur kuch items bina number ke hain. Upar saare unique concepts cover kiye gaye hain — kuch chhoota nahi hai.

Best System Design Interview Questions (10)

Ye concept-based questions aksar telephonic round me puche jaate hain. Har question ke saath Hinglish me chhota jawab-sketch hai — interview me tumhe isi ko apne shabdo me, example ke saath bolna hai.

  1. API Gateway aur Load Balancer me difference? — Gateway single entry point hai (auth, rate limiting, routing), Load Balancer traffic baant-ta hai. Dono saath kaam karte hain. Detail me padho
  2. Reverse Proxy aur Forward Proxy me difference? — Forward proxy client ko chhupata hai, reverse proxy server ko. Detail me padho
  3. Horizontal scaling vs vertical scaling? — Vertical = ek machine powerful banao; Horizontal = machines jodo. Horizontal practically unlimited aur fault-tolerant hai. Detail me padho
  4. Microservices vs Monolithic architecture? — Monolith simple aur tez shuruaat ke liye; microservices bade, fast-changing systems ke liye, lekin complexity ke saath. Detail me padho
  5. Vertical vs horizontal partitioning (sharding) me difference? — Vertical partitioning matlab columns/tables alag karna; horizontal matlab rows ko tukdo me baantna (sharding). Detail me padho
  6. Rate Limiter kya hai, kaise kaam karta hai? — Requests ki speed control karta hai; Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, Fixed/Sliding Window algorithms. Detail me padho
  7. Single Sign-On (SSO) kaise kaam karta hai? — Ek baar login, saari apps me access; Identity Provider token deta hai. Detail me padho
  8. Apache Kafka kaise kaam karta hai, itna fast kyun hai? — Sequential disk writes, zero-copy, batching, partitioning. Detail me padho
  9. Kafka, ActiveMQ aur RabbitMQ me difference? — Kafka high-throughput streaming, RabbitMQ routing aur workflows, ActiveMQ Java/JMS ecosystem. Detail me padho
  10. JWT, OAuth aur SAML me difference? — JWT token format hai, OAuth authorization framework hai, SAML enterprise SSO protocol hai. Detail me padho
Interview tip: in questions ka ek-line jawab yaad karne se kuch nahi hoga. Har ek par 2 minute bolne ki practice karo — definition, kaise kaam karta hai, kab use karte hain, trade-offs. Wahi interviewer ko impress karta hai.

Theory aur Concept based Questions (7)

Ye theory questions concepts ki gehri samajh check karte hain. Har ek ke saath Hinglish explanation aur original article ka link hai.

  • ActiveMQ, Kafka aur RabbitMQ me difference — Kafka streaming aur high throughput ke liye, RabbitMQ complex routing aur guaranteed delivery ke liye, ActiveMQ legacy Java systems ke liye. Chuno use-case se, naam se nahi.
  • Distributed data structures aur algorithms — Bloom Filter, consistent hashing, vector clocks, gossip protocol — ye woh data structures hain jo distributed systems ko kaam karte hain. Section 13 me inme se kuch detail me samjhaye gaye hain.
  • Microservices vs Monolithic Architecture — Monolith se shuru karo, jab team badi ho aur services alag scale karni ho tab microservices me todo. Galat time par microservices banana sabse badi galti hai.
  • API Gateway vs Load Balancer — Dono traffic handle karte hain, lekin Gateway application-level kaam (auth, rate limit) karta hai aur Load Balancer network-level traffic baant-ta hai.
  • Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling — Vertical aasan lekin limit hai; horizontal mushkil lekin practically unlimited. Real systems dono ka mix use karte hain.
  • Forward proxy vs reverse proxy — Kaun kisko chhupata hai, yahi ek line me difference hai: forward client ko, reverse server ko.
  • 9 Caching Strategies — Cache-Aside, Read-Through, Write-Through, Write-Behind, Write-Around, Refresh-Ahead aur bhi — har strategy ka apna use-case aur apna trade-off hai. Interview me "kaunsi strategy kab" poochte hain.

Best System Design Interview Problems (14)

Ye System Design interviews ka "holy grail" hai — sabse popular practice problems. Har problem ke saath Hinglish me approach ka hint hai — poora solution linked article me hai, lekin approach yahan samajh lo to solution khud ban jayega.

  • YouTube Design — Video upload, storage, streaming, recommendations. Socho: video kaise store hogi, CDN kaise kaam karega, views ka counter kaise consistent rahega.
  • URL Shortener — Sabse pehla problem. Base62 encoding, hash collisions, database design, aur scale ka andaza (kitne URLs per day).
  • Real-Time Gaming Leaderboard — Scores real-time update hone chahiye. Sorted sets (Redis) aur sharding ka classic use-case.
  • WhatsApp Design — Real-time messaging, delivery receipts, online status, group chats. WebSockets aur message queues ka use.
  • Parking Lot Design — Ye low-level design ki taraf zyada hai — classes, slots, ticketing. LLD+HLD dono ki practice hoti hai.
  • Design a LMS (Learning Management System) — Courses, videos, quizzes, progress tracking — ek poora product design karo.
  • Instagram Design — Photo upload, feed generation, followers. Feed kaise banegi — push vs pull model samajhna zaroori hai.
  • TinyURL Design — URL shortener ka hi doosra naam — is problem ko do tareeke se design karke dekho.
  • Real-Time Live Comments — Live stream par comments real-time aane chahiye — WebSockets, fan-out, moderation.
  • Distributed Counter — Likes/views jaisa counter jise lakhon log ek saath badha rahe hon — sharding aur eventual consistency ka sawal.
  • Real Time Presence Platform — Kaun online hai, kaun typing kar raha hai — presence information real-time me.
  • 50+ System Design Problems — Ek hi jagah 50 se zyada problems ki list — roz ek problem uthao.
  • Spotify Design — Music streaming, playlists, recommendations — audio storage aur delivery ka design.
  • Rate Limiter — Rate limiter khud ek design problem hai — algorithms (token bucket, sliding window) ke saath poora system design karo.
Practice ka tareeka: har problem par 45 minute ka timer lagao. Pehle requirements likho, phir scale ka andaza (QPS, storage), phir API, phir high-level design, phir deep-dive, phir bottlenecks aur trade-offs. Bina timer ke practice karna interview ki taiyaari nahi hai.

Distributed Data Structures and Algorithms (4)

Ye woh data structures aur algorithms hain jo distributed systems ko possible banate hain. Normal DSA se alag, ye network par bante hue systems ke liye bane hain.

Bloom Filter

Bloom Filter ek space-efficient data structure hai jo batata hai ki koi element shayad set me hai ya pakka nahi hai. Matlab: agar Bloom Filter kehta hai "nahi hai" to 100% nahi hai; agar kehta hai "hai" to ho bhi sakta hai, nahi bhi (false positive possible hai). Use: database query karne se pehle check karna ki key hai bhi ya nahi — bade systems me isse lakhon bekaar DB queries bachte hain. Detail me padho

Actor Model

Actor Model me system chhote independent "actors" se banta hai — har actor ka apna state hota hai, aur actors ek dusre se sirf messages bhej kar baat karte hain, shared memory se nahi. Isse concurrency ki problems (locks, race conditions) khatm ho jaati hain. Erlang, Akka jaise systems isi par chalte hain. Detail me padho

Gossip Protocol

Gossip Protocol me nodes ek dusre ko information "afwah" ki tarah failate hain — har node kuch random nodes ko apni jaankari bhejta hai, wo aage bhejta hain, aur kuch hi rounds me saara cluster update ho jaata hai. Failure detection aur cluster membership ke liye use hota hai (Cassandra, Consul). Detail me padho

Quotient Filter

Quotient Filter Bloom Filter jaisa hi hai — membership check karta hai — lekin isme ek extra fayda hai: ye deletion bhi support karta hai aur cache-friendly hota hai. Space kam leta hai aur modern systems me Bloom Filter ke alternative ke roop me use hota hai. Detail me padho

Best System Design Papers — Amazon Dynamo

Research papers padhna interview ke liye zaroori nahi hai, lekin jo systems aaj use hote hain, wo inhi papers se nikle hain. README me ek paper hai — aur wo bahut important hai.

Amazon Dynamo (2007)

Amazon Dynamo paper — Is paper ne Amazon ke shopping cart aur session data ke liye ek highly available key-value store design kiya tha. Isi paper se aaj ka Amazon DynamoDB nikla hai.

Is paper ke 4 core ideas

  • Consistent Hashing — Data ko nodes par aise baanto ki node add/remove karne par kam se kam data move ho. (Section 06 me detail me samjhaya hai.)
  • Vector Clocks — Har data version ke saath ek clock rakho taaki pata chale kaunsa version naya hai aur kahan conflict hai.
  • Sloppy Quorum — Strict quorum ki jagah thodi dheel: agar pehle 3 nodes me se koi down hai to agle healthy node par likh do — availability pehle, consistency baad me sync hogi.
  • Hinted Handoff — Down node ka data temporarily dusre node par rakh do; jab wo wapas aaye to data usko de do.

Interview me is paper ka naam lena hi kaafi nahi — ye 4 ideas samajh lo, to tum "eventual consistency" aur "high availability" par koi bhi sawal handle kar sakte ho.

System Design Patterns — Service Discovery

Design patterns woh repeat hone wale solutions hain jo har distributed system me kaam aate hain. README ke is section me ek pattern hai.

Service Discovery

Microservices me services ke addresses (IP/port) badalte rehte hain — services up-down hoti hain, scale hoti hain. Service Discovery ka matlab hai: koi service dusri service ko kaise dhoondhe? Iske liye ek registry hoti hai jahan har service apna address register karti hai, aur dusri services wahan se lookup karti hain. Do tareeke hain: client-side discovery (client registry se poochta hai) aur server-side discovery (load balancer registry se poochta hai). Tools: Consul, Eureka, etcd. Detail me padho

Aur patterns — Circuit Breaker, Saga, CQRS, Event-Driven — Section 06 me detail me samjhaye gaye hain.

FInterview FAQs

Interview FAQs (36)

System Design interview ke aas-paas ke sabse zyada puche jaane wale sawaal — taiyaari, resources, aur interview ke din ke liye.

Q01System Design interview ki taiyaari kahan se shuru karun?
Bilkul zero se shuru kar rahe ho to pehle ek structured course lo — ByteByteGo ya Codemia — aur saath me Section 06 ke basics padho. Sirf videos dekhna kaafi nahi; har concept ke baad khud se ek chhota design banao. Pehle 2 hafte sirf seekhne me lagao, phir problems practice karo.
Q02Course lu ya book padhun — kya better hai?
Dono ka apna kaam hai. Course se structure milta hai aur jaldi samajh aata hai; book se gehrai milti hai. Best combo: pehle Grokking the System Design Interview jaisa course, phir System Design Interview kitab, phir Designing Data-Intensive Applications. Sirf ek par depend mat raho.
Q03Kitne time me System Design interview ki taiyaari ho jaati hai?
Background par depend karta hai. Agar tumne pehle backend systems banaye hain to 4-6 hafte focused taiyaari kaafi hai. Bilkul naye ho to 2-3 mahine lag sakte hain. Roz 1-2 ghante consistent practice, ek din me 8 ghante se behtar hai.
Q04Free resources se taiyaari ho sakti hai?
Haan, bilkul. GitHub par free repos, Exponent ke free mock interviews, ByteByteGo ke free guides, aur is repo ke saare links — in sab se poori taiyaari ho sakti hai. Paid course sirf structure aur speed ke liye hai, knowledge free me bhi milta hai.
Q05Sabse pehle kaunsi book padhni chahiye?
System Design Interview wali kitab — ye interview framework aur classic problems ke liye best starting point hai. Uske baad Designing Data-Intensive Applications — ye gehrai ke liye hai. ML roles ke liye Machine Learning System Design Interview add karo.
Q06System Design interview me sabse badi galti kya hoti hai?
Requirements pooche bina design shuru kar dena. Interviewer jaan-bujh kar vague sawal deta hai — pehle 5 minute requirements aur scale samajhne me lagao. Doosri badi galti: trade-offs na batana. Har decision ke peeche 'kyun' hona chahiye.
Q07Back-of-the-envelope calculation kyun zaroori hai?
Ye interviewer ko batata hai ki tumhe scale ki samajh hai. QPS, storage aur bandwidth ka andaza lagaye bina design karna andhere me teer chalana hai. Lab 2 ka calculator use karke practice karo — 2-3 baar karne ke baad numbers zubani yaad ho jaate hain.
Q08Microservices kab use karne chahiye aur kab nahi?
Jab team badi ho, services alag-alag scale karni hon, aur alag teams alag parts par kaam karein — tab microservices. Chhote app, chhoti team, ya jaldi launch karna ho to monolith better hai. Prime Video ka example yaad rakho — microservices se wapas monolith jaakar unhone bachat ki thi.
Q09Caching ke liye kaunsi strategy kab use karni hai?
Read-heavy aur thoda purana data chale to Cache-Aside + TTL. Har write par fresh data chahiye to Write-Through. Write-heavy aur tez writes chahiye to Write-Behind (data loss ka risk samajh kar). Interview me strategy ke saath trade-off bhi batao.
Q10Rate Limiter ke liye kaunsa algorithm best hai?
Token Bucket ya Sliding Window — kyunki Fixed Window me boundary problem hoti hai (window badalte hi 2x requests nikal jaati hain). Lab 4 ka simulator ye difference saaf dikhata hai.
Q11Consistent Hashing interview me kyun poochte hain?
Kyunki ye caching aur distributed storage ka core hai. Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum samajhte ho ki node add/remove karne par normal hashing me saara data kyun move hota hai aur consistent hashing ise kaise rokta hai. Lab 5 me live dekh sakte ho.
Q12Kafka aur RabbitMQ me se kab kaunsa chunna chahiye?
High-throughput event streaming aur logs ke liye Kafka. Complex routing, per-message acknowledgement aur traditional queue workflows ke liye RabbitMQ. Interview me 'kab kaunsa' ka jawab use-case se do, naam se nahi.
Q13JWT aur Session me se kya better hai?
Dono ke trade-offs hain. JWT stateless hai — scale karna aasan, lekin revoke karna mushkil. Session revoke karna aasan hai, lekin server par state rakhni padti hai. Interview me dono ke fayde-nuksan batao, ek ko 'best' mat kaho.
Q14System Design problems kaise practice karun?
Roz ek problem, 45 minute ka timer. Pehle requirements likho, phir scale ka andaza, phir API, phir high-level design, phir deep-dive, phir bottlenecks aur trade-offs. Bina timer ke practice interview ki taiyaari nahi hai. Lab 7 ka randomizer use karo.
Q15URL Shortener design me sabse important cheez kya hai?
ID generation — unique, short, aur collision-free. Base62 encoding standard jawab hai. Uske baad database design (URL mapping store karna) aur scale ka andaza (kitne URLs per day, kitna storage).
Q16WhatsApp jaisa chat system kaise design karte hain?
Real-time messaging ke liye WebSockets, messages ke liye message queue, delivery receipts aur online status ke liye presence service. Group chats me fan-out ka dhyaan rakho — ek message lakhon users tak kaise pahunchega.
Q17Instagram feed — push ya pull model?
Dono ka mix hota hai. Celebrities (zyada followers) ke liye pull model — feed khulte hi compute karo. Normal users ke liye push model — post karte hi followers ki feed me daal do. Interview me dono ke trade-offs batao.
Q18Database sharding me sabse mushkil hissa kya hai?
Shard key chunna aur cross-shard queries. Galat shard key se ek shard overload ho jaata hai (hotspot). Cross-shard joins mushkil hote hain — isliye sharding se pehle socho ki queries kaisi hongi.
Q19CAP theorem interview me kaise samjhau?
CAP matlab Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance — teeno me se ek saath sirf do mil sakte hain. Partition hone par tumhe Consistency ya Availability me se ek chunna padta hai. Real systems me choice use-case par based hoti hai — banking me consistency, social feed me availability.
Q20Eventual consistency matlab kya hai?
Matlab data turant nahi, thodi der me saari jagah same ho jayega. Writes tez hote hain, lekin padhne par thoda purana data dikh sakta hai. Social media likes, comments — in sab me eventual consistency chalti hai. Banking me nahi.
Q21Saga pattern kab use karte hain?
Jab ek transaction multiple microservices me phaila ho aur koi step fail ho jaye. Har step ke saath compensating action hoti hai — jaise payment fail ho to refund. Choreography ya orchestration — dono tareeke interview me batao.
Q22Idempotency kyun zaroori hai?
Network me request dobara bhi pahunch sakti hai (retry). Agar operation idempotent nahi hai to paise do baar kat sakte hain ya order do baar ban sakta hai. Isliye har request ko unique idempotency key do.
Q23Circuit Breaker ka real example kya hai?
Ghar ka MCB jaisa — zyada load aate hi trip kar jaata hai taaki aage nuksan na ho. Software me: agar ek service baar-baar fail ho rahi hai to use call karna band kar do aur fallback do. Ye cascading failures rokta hai.
Q24Service Discovery kyun chahiye?
Microservices me services ke IP/port badalte rehte hain. Bina discovery ke ek service dusri ko dhoondhe kaise? Registry (Consul, Eureka) me har service apna address register karti hai. Client-side ya server-side — dono tareeke hote hain.
Q25Bloom Filter kahan use hota hai?
Database query karne se pehle check karna ki key hai bhi ya nahi. Agar Bloom Filter kehta hai 'nahi hai' to 100% nahi hai — bekaar DB query bach jaati hai. Cassandra aur bade databases isi ka use karte hain.
Q26Dynamo paper kyun important hai?
Isi paper se consistent hashing, vector clocks, sloppy quorum aur hinted handoff jaise ideas aaye — aur isi par Amazon DynamoDB bana. Interview me 'high availability kaise laate ho' ka jawab is paper se nikalta hai.
Q27Mock interviews kab se dena shuru karun?
Jab tum 4-5 problems khud se solve kar chuke ho. Usse pehle mock dena time waste hai — pehle basics aur framework pakka karo. Exponent ke free peer mocks se shuru karo, phir paid mocks.
Q28Target company ka engineering blog kyun padhna chahiye?
Kyunki interview questions aksar usi domain ke hote hain. Agar tumhe pata hai ki Netflix microservices kaise use karta hai ya Uber matching kaise karta hai, to tumhare jawab me woh depth dikhegi jo sirf theory padhne wale me nahi hoti.
Q29System Design ke saath Low-Level Design bhi aana chahiye?
Senior roles me HLD (high-level) zyada poochte hain, lekin kuch companies (khaas taur par India me) LLD bhi poochti hain — jaise Parking Lot design. Is repo ke problems me Parking Lot hai, usse LLD ki practice ho jaati hai.
Q30Cheat sheets se kaam chal jayega?
Nahi — cheat sheet sirf revision ke liye hai. Pehle concepts samjho, phir problems practice karo, aur aakhir me cheat sheet se revise karo. Sirf cheat sheet ratne wala interviewer ke pehle deep-dive question par atak jaata hai.
Q31Grokking the System Design Interview course lena chahiye?
Ye sabse popular course hai aur beginners ke liye achha hai. Lekin course ke saath-saath khud problems solve karo — sirf course dekh kar interview nahi nikalta. Reviews Section 18 me hain, pehle padh lo.
Q32System Design seekhne me sabse badi galti kya hai?
Sirf padhna aur kabhi khud design na karna. System Design haath se karne ki cheez hai — har concept ke baad ek problem uthao aur khud se design banao. Jo design tumne khud banaya hai, wo interview me yaad rehta hai.
Q33Interview me agar design atak jaye to kya karun?
Ruko mat — interviewer se sawal poocho. 'Is feature ki priority kya hai?' ya 'Scale kitna hai?' — ye sawal poochna kamzori nahi, samajhdari hai. Interviewer tumhari soch dekh raha hai, final diagram nahi.
Q34Consistency models — strong vs eventual — kab kaunsa?
Paise, inventory, booking jaise cases me strong consistency — galat data ka matlab nuksan. Social feed, likes, comments me eventual consistency chalti hai — thoda purana data dikhna acceptable hai. Interview me example ke saath batao.
Q35API Gateway aur Load Balancer ek hi cheez hain?
Nahi. Gateway application-level kaam karta hai — authentication, rate limiting, routing. Load Balancer network-level traffic baant-ta hai. Dono saath me kaam karte hain, aur interview me dono ka difference aksar poochte hain.
Q36Shuruaat me kaunsa course best hai — ByteByteGo ya Grokking?
Dono achhe hain. ByteByteGo visual hai — diagrams se samajhna aasan. Grokking step-by-step solutions ke liye best hai. Agar diagrams se seekhte ho to ByteByteGo, agar solutions padh kar seekhte ho to Grokking. Budget ho to dono ka combo best hai.
